library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Astrand_2019_ticagrelor"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Astrand_2019_ticagrelor"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13812> (open access, PMC6339964)

Astrand 2019 pooled two AstraZeneca studies, ONSET/OFFSET (stable coronary
artery disease, CAD) and the PEGASUS-TIMI 54 platelet function substudy (prior
myocardial infarction, MI), to relate ticagrelor exposure to platelet
reactivity measured as VerifyNow P2Y12 reaction units (PRU). Ticagrelor and its
active metabolite AR-C124910XX were modelled jointly; platelet inhibition is a
direct sigmoid Emax function of the ticagrelor concentration alone. The
authors tested the sum of parent and metabolite as the driver and kept
ticagrelor alone (OFV difference 3.6).

**Units.** Doses are in mg and concentrations in nmol/L, as in the paper. The
model converts with the ticagrelor molecular weight, 522.57 g/mol. The
metabolite states hold ticagrelor-equivalent mass, so the molar fraction
`fm` carries straight through and the metabolite's own molecular weight is not
needed.

# Population

ONSET/OFFSET randomised 123 mainly white (88%) patients with stable CAD to
ticagrelor 180 mg then 90 mg twice daily (n = 57), clopidogrel 600 mg then 75
mg once daily (n = 54, not modelled) or placebo (n = 12) for about six weeks.
The PEGASUS-TIMI 54 platelet function substudy randomised 180 mainly white
(93%) patients with an MI 1-3 years earlier to placebo (n = 64), ticagrelor 60
mg (n = 58) or 90 mg (n = 58) twice daily, sampled before and 2 h after a dose
after at least four months of treatment. All patients took aspirin. The
analysis used 871 ticagrelor, 872 AR-C124910XX and 954 PRU measurements
(Astrand 2019 Methods and Table 1). Age, weight and sex are not reported in the
article, and no demographic covariate entered the model.

The only covariate is the study indicator `STUDY_PEGASUS` (1 = PEGASUS-TIMI 54
prior-MI patient). It switches on a 0.48 h absorption lag and lowers the PRU
baseline from 311 to 261.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Astrand_2019_ticagrelor")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Astrand_2019_ticagrelor.R`; this table collects
them. All values are from Astrand 2019 Table 2 unless stated.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL/F) | 16.6 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q/F) | 10.4 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (Vc/F) | 156 L | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (Vp/F) | 55.8 L | Table 2 |
| `lktr` (KTR) | 10.1 1/h | Table 2 |
| `ltlag` (lag, prior MI only) | 0.48 h | Table 2, 'Absorption lag time prior MI' |
| `lfdepot` (Frel) | 1, fixed | Table 2, '1 FIX' |
| `lcl_tam` (CLm/F) | 10.2 L/h | Table 2 |
| `fm` (Fm) | 0.22, fixed | Table 2 '0.22 FIX'; Methods |
| `lq_tam` (Qm/F) | 4.41 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc_tam` (Vcm/F) | 7.04 L | Table 2 |
| `lvp_tam` (Vpm/F) | 42.3 L | Table 2 |
| `rbase` (PRU baseline, ONSET/OFFSET) | 311 | Table 2; Results |
| `rbase_pegasus` (PRU baseline, PEGASUS) | 261 | Table 2; Results |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 116 nmol/L | Table 2; Abstract |
| `logitemax` (Emax) | logit(0.985) | Table 2, Emax 98.5% derived from the estimated logit |
| `hill` (gamma) | 1.59 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl`, `etalq`, `etalktr`, `etalfdepot` | 0.24^2, 0.95^2, 0.54^2, 0.32^2 | Table 2 BSV column (24, 95, 54, 32%) |
| `etalcl_tam`, `etalvp_tam` | 0.28^2, 0.37^2 | Table 2 BSV column (28, 37%) |
| `etarbase` + `etalec50` | 35^2, 0.33 * 35 * 0.66, 0.66^2 | Table 2: PRU baseline SD 35 (additive), EC50 66%, correlation 0.33 |
| `etalogitemax` | 2.2^2 | Table 2: Emax BSV 2.2, SD on the logit scale (footnote) |
| `propSd`, `propSd_tam` | 0.32, 0.26 | Table 2 proportional residual errors |
| `propSd_PRU`, `powExp_PRU` | 47.6 / 300^0.48, 0.48 | Table 2 and footnote: SD = (PRU/300)^alpha * 47.6 |
| Erlang absorption, 8 transits, one KTR | -- | Results, 'Ticagrelor population PK model' |
| Two-compartment parent and metabolite, Fm of CL/F forms metabolite | -- | Methods, 'Population PK/PD model development' |
| `PRU = PRU_baseline * (1 - Emax * C^gamma / (EC50^gamma + C^gamma))` | -- | Results equation |
| Molecular weight 522.57 g/mol | -- | Not printed; reproduces the printed steady-state averages exactly (below) |

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Astrand_2019_ticagrelor")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
```

# Event-table helpers

The model has three endpoints (`Cc`, `Cc_tam`, `PRU`), so observation rows name
the `central` ODE state together with `dvid = 1L`. Concentrations and the
inhibition fraction `inhib` are returned on every row regardless.

```{r helpers}
make_events <- function(ids, dose_mg, n_doses, ii, obs_times, pegasus) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = ii * (seq_len(n_doses) - 1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(STUDY_PEGASUS = pegasus)
}

solve_df <- function(model, events, keep = NULL) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    model, events = events, keep = keep,
    useLinCmt = FALSE, maxsteps = 5e5
  ))
}
```

# Typical-value checks against printed numbers

The Results print three deterministic quantities that pin the structure: the
average steady-state concentration for 60 and 90 mg twice daily (576 and 864
nmol/L) and the terminal half-lives of ticagrelor and AR-C124910XX (10.2 and
9.6 h, Discussion). Since `Css,av = F * Dose / (CL/F * tau)`, the first pair
also fixes the molecular weight used for the nmol/L conversion.

```{r typical-checks}
css_typ <- lapply(c(60, 90), function(d) {
  ev <- make_events(1L, d, 40, 12, seq(468, 480, by = 0.01), pegasus = 0)
  s <- solve_df(typ, ev)
  data.frame(dose = d, css_av = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$Cc, -1) + tail(s$Cc, -1)) / 2) / 12)
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
css_typ$published <- c(576, 864)
knitr::kable(
  css_typ |> dplyr::rename("Dose (mg BID)" = dose, "Css,av simulated (nmol/L)" = css_av,
                           "Css,av published (nmol/L)" = published),
  digits = 1
)

# Terminal half-life of each two-compartment disposition from its eigenvalues.
p <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$theta
half_life <- function(cl, q, vc, vp) {
  k10 <- cl / vc; k12 <- q / vc; k21 <- q / vp
  s <- k10 + k12 + k21
  beta <- (s - sqrt(s^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
  log(2) / beta
}
t_half <- c(
  ticagrelor = half_life(exp(p[["lcl"]]), exp(p[["lq"]]), exp(p[["lvc"]]), exp(p[["lvp"]])),
  AR_C124910XX = half_life(exp(p[["lcl_tam"]]), exp(p[["lq_tam"]]), exp(p[["lvc_tam"]]), exp(p[["lvp_tam"]]))
)
round(t_half, 2)

# Typical-value peak after the 180 mg loading dose (stable CAD, no lag).
typ_ld <- solve_df(typ, make_events(1L, 180, 1, 24, seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), pegasus = 0))
cmax_typ <- max(typ_ld$Cc)
round(cmax_typ)

stopifnot(
  abs(css_typ$css_av / css_typ$published - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(t_half[["ticagrelor"]] - 10.2) < 0.1,
  abs(t_half[["AR_C124910XX"]] - 9.6) < 0.15,
  # Printed median Cmax 2096 nmol/L; the deterministic peak is about 8% lower
  # (see the PKNCA section).
  abs(cmax_typ / 2096 - 1) < 0.10
)
```

Both steady-state averages match to within rounding, and the half-lives
(10.18 and 9.67 h) match the Discussion's 10.2 and 9.6 h.

# Concentration-response (replicates Figure 3)

The Results state that "80% median platelet inhibition (IQR: 66-86%) ... was
on average reached at ticagrelor concentrations of 344 nmol/L". The spread
comes only from the EC50 and Emax random effects, so it can be reproduced
directly from the model's omega matrix. It also tests how the Table 2 'BSV'
column was read: the logit-scale Emax entry of 2.2 is taken as an SD, as the
table footnote states.

```{r conc-response}
om <- ui$omega
set.seed(20190201)
n_pd <- 20000
eta_ec50 <- rnorm(n_pd, 0, sqrt(om["etalec50", "etalec50"]))
eta_emax <- rnorm(n_pd, 0, sqrt(om["etalogitemax", "etalogitemax"]))
ec50_i <- exp(p[["lec50"]] + eta_ec50)
emax_i <- plogis(p[["logitemax"]] + eta_emax)
inhib_at <- function(conc) emax_i * conc^p[["hill"]] / (ec50_i^p[["hill"]] + conc^p[["hill"]])

q344 <- 100 * quantile(inhib_at(344), c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
round(q344, 1)
stopifnot(abs(q344[["50%"]] - 80) < 3, abs(q344[["25%"]] - 66) < 4)

conc_grid <- c(0, exp(seq(log(1), log(6000), length.out = 120)))
curve <- lapply(conc_grid, function(cc) {
  x <- 100 * inhib_at(cc)
  data.frame(conc = cc, median = median(x), lo = quantile(x, 0.025), hi = quantile(x, 0.975))
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()

ggplot(curve, aes(conc + 1, median)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Ticagrelor plasma concentration + 1 (nmol/L)", y = "PRU inhibition (%)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Astrand 2019: median and 95% interval over EC50 and Emax variability.")
```

The simulated quartiles at 344 nmol/L are close to the published 66, 80 and 86%.
Figure 3's shaded band is narrower at high concentrations than this one; the
band in the paper is not defined beyond "95% prediction interval", and the
model's logit-normal Emax (SD 2.2) gives about 5% of patients a maximal
inhibition below 64%, which is what the steady-state quantiles below require.

# Loading dose in stable CAD and prior MI patients (replicates Figures 1 and 2)

```{r loading-dose}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
n_per_arm <- 200
obs_ld <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2, 2.25, 2.5, 2.75, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)
ev_ld <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1:n_per_arm, 180, 1, 24, obs_ld, pegasus = 0) |> dplyr::mutate(population = "Stable CAD"),
  make_events(n_per_arm + 1:n_per_arm, 180, 1, 24, obs_ld, pegasus = 1) |> dplyr::mutate(population = "Prior MI")
)
sim_ld <- solve_df(ui, ev_ld, keep = "population")

sim_ld |>
  dplyr::filter(population == "Stable CAD") |>
  dplyr::select(time, Cc, PRU) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, PRU)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(name, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p10 = quantile(value, 0.1), p50 = median(value), p90 = quantile(value, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = labeller(name = c(Cc = "Ticagrelor (nmol/L)", PRU = "PRU (with residual error)"))) +
  labs(x = "Time after the 180 mg loading dose (h)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the upper-left panels of Figures 1 and 2 of Astrand 2019: median and 10th-90th percentiles.")
```

The Results report that the median maximal PRU inhibition after the 180 mg
loading dose was 96% (IQR 91-98%), reached on average at 1.8 h in CAD and
2.4 h in prior MI patients. The simulated values use the individual
predictions (no residual error). The paper's "on average" times are compared
with the simulated mean times (1.7 and 2.2 h here); the prior-MI delay comes
from the 0.48 h lag.

```{r ld-peak}
peak <- sim_ld |>
  dplyr::group_by(population, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(max_inhib = 100 * max(inhib), t_max_inhib = time[which.max(inhib)], .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::group_by(population) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median max inhibition (%)` = median(max_inhib),
    `Q1 (%)` = quantile(max_inhib, 0.25),
    `Q3 (%)` = quantile(max_inhib, 0.75),
    `Mean time of max inhibition (h)` = mean(t_max_inhib),
    `Median time of max inhibition (h)` = median(t_max_inhib)
  )
knitr::kable(peak, digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  all(abs(peak$`Median max inhibition (%)` - 96) < 3),
  peak$`Median time of max inhibition (h)`[peak$population == "Prior MI"] >
    peak$`Median time of max inhibition (h)`[peak$population == "Stable CAD"]
)
```

# Steady-state dose response (replicates Figure 4)

The paper simulated 15-90 mg twice daily at steady state and summarised PRU
inhibition 2 h after a dose and at the 12 h trough. Fourteen doses (7 days,
about 16 terminal half-lives) reach steady state. The paper does not say which
population was simulated; inhibition does not depend on the PRU baseline, and
the lag time hardly moves steady-state concentrations, so the stable-CAD
setting is used.

```{r dose-response}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(4)
doses <- c(15, 30, 45, 60, 90)
ev_dr <- lapply(seq_along(doses), function(i) {
  make_events((i - 1) * n_per_arm + 1:n_per_arm, doses[i], 14, 12, c(158, 168), pegasus = 0) |>
    dplyr::mutate(dose = doses[i])
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()
sim_dr <- solve_df(ui, ev_dr, keep = "dose") |>
  dplyr::mutate(when = ifelse(time == 158, "2 h post-dose", "Trough 12 h after dose"),
                inhib_pct = 100 * inhib)

ggplot(sim_dr, aes(factor(dose), inhib_pct)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, coef = 0) +
  stat_summary(fun.min = function(x) quantile(x, 0.05), fun.max = function(x) quantile(x, 0.95),
               fun = median, geom = "linerange") +
  facet_wrap(~when) +
  labs(x = "Dose (mg twice daily)", y = "PRU inhibition (%)",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Astrand 2019: box = IQR, whiskers = 5th-95th percentiles.")
```

The Results give medians and IQRs for 30-90 mg, and the proportion of patients
below 70% inhibition at the trough.

```{r dose-response-table}
published_dr <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose, ~when, ~pub_median, ~pub_q1, ~pub_q3,
  90, "2 h post-dose", 94, 87, 97,
  90, "Trough 12 h after dose", 87, 73, 93,
  60, "2 h post-dose", 92, 83, 96,
  60, "Trough 12 h after dose", 80, 62, 90,
  45, "2 h post-dose", 89, 78, 95,
  45, "Trough 12 h after dose", 73, 53, 86,
  30, "2 h post-dose", 83, 68, 91,
  30, "Trough 12 h after dose", 60, 39, 77
)
published_below70 <- tibble::tibble(dose = c(90, 60, 45, 30), pub_below70 = c(22, 34, 46, 63))

sim_dr_summary <- sim_dr |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, when) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    sim_median = median(inhib_pct), sim_q1 = quantile(inhib_pct, 0.25),
    sim_q3 = quantile(inhib_pct, 0.75), sim_below70 = 100 * mean(inhib_pct < 70),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
dr_cmp <- published_dr |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_dr_summary, by = c("dose", "when")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(published_below70, by = "dose") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pub_below70 = ifelse(when == "Trough 12 h after dose", pub_below70, NA),
    sim_below70 = ifelse(when == "Trough 12 h after dose", sim_below70, NA)
  )
dr_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose, "Time" = when,
    "Published median" = pub_median, "Published Q1" = pub_q1, "Published Q3" = pub_q3,
    "Simulated median" = sim_median, "Simulated Q1" = sim_q1, "Simulated Q3" = sim_q3,
    "Simulated % < 70" = sim_below70, "Published % < 70" = pub_below70
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "PRU inhibition (%) at steady state: simulated versus Astrand 2019 Results.")

# Centre and robust-quantile assertions only (200 subjects per arm).
stopifnot(
  max(abs(dr_cmp$sim_median - dr_cmp$pub_median)) < 5,
  max(abs(dr_cmp$sim_q1 - dr_cmp$pub_q1)) < 8,
  max(abs(dr_cmp$sim_q3 - dr_cmp$pub_q3)) < 5
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the simulated ticagrelor profiles, compared with
the two exposure numbers in the Results: median Cmax after the 180 mg loading
dose (2096 nmol/L, CAD patients) and the steady-state average concentration
for 60 and 90 mg twice daily (576 and 864 nmol/L).

```{r pknca-single}
conc_ld <- sim_ld |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste("180 mg loading dose,", population)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_ld <- ev_ld |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste("180 mg loading dose,", population)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ld, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ld, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals_ld <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_ld <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_ld))
summary(nca_ld)
```

```{r pknca-ss}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(60)
obs_ss <- 156 + c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)
ev_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(1:n_per_arm, 60, 14, 12, obs_ss, pegasus = 1) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "60 mg BID"),
  make_events(n_per_arm + 1:n_per_arm, 90, 14, 12, obs_ss, pegasus = 1) |> dplyr::mutate(treatment = "90 mg BID")
)
sim_ss <- solve_df(ui, ev_ss, keep = "treatment")

# Re-base the last dosing interval to start at time 0.
conc_ss <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = time - 156) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_ss <- ev_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 156) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
intervals_ss <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, cmax = TRUE, cav = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_ss <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals_ss
))
summary(nca_ss)
```

```{r nca-compare}
simulated_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_ld) |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "180 mg loading dose, Stable CAD", PPTESTCD == "cmax"),
  as.data.frame(nca_ss) |> dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cav")
) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~cav,
  "180 mg loading dose, Stable CAD", 2096, NA,
  "60 mg BID", NA, 576,
  "90 mg BID", NA, 864
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated_nca,
  reference = published_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "nmol/L", cav = "nmol/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated median NCA versus the medians printed in the Astrand 2019 Results.")

sim_med <- simulated_nca |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(
  # The cohort median sits 10-13% below the printed value (explained below);
  # the bound leaves room for cohort-to-cohort spread.
  abs(sim_med$med[sim_med$PPTESTCD == "cmax"] / 2096 - 1) < 0.20,
  all(abs(sim_med$med[sim_med$PPTESTCD == "cav"] / c(576, 864) - 1) < 0.15)
)
```

The steady-state averages from NCA are cohort medians; the typical-value
calculation above reproduces the printed 576 and 864 nmol/L exactly.

The simulated median Cmax after the 180 mg loading dose is about 10% below the
printed 2096 nmol/L. The typical-value Cmax is about 1920 nmol/L, and the
between-subject variability lowers the median of the individual-prediction
peaks slightly (to about 1870 nmol/L in a 3000-subject run) rather than raising
it. Reading the log-normal BSV column as `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` instead
changes the median by less than 1%. Taking the largest of the residual-error
observations at the ONSET/OFFSET sampling times (0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 24 h)
gives about 1970 nmol/L. The paper does not say how its median Cmax was
derived, so the gap is reported rather than explained; the parameters are not
adjusted to close it.

# Metabolite exposure

The Discussion states the AR-C124910XX exposure was "approximately one third of
the ticagrelor exposure". In molar terms the steady-state AUC ratio is
`Fm * (CL/F) / (CLm/F) = 0.22 * 16.6 / 10.2 = 0.36`.

```{r metabolite}
auc_ratio <- sim_ss |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(ratio = sum(Cc_tam) / sum(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_ratio = median(ratio))
auc_ratio
stopifnot(abs(auc_ratio$median_ratio - 0.36) < 0.05)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **BSV scale.** Table 2's 'BSV (%)' column for the log-normal etas (CL/F,
  Q/F, KTR, Frel, CLm/F, Vpm/F, EC50) is read as `sqrt(omega^2) * 100`, so
  `omega^2 = (BSV/100)^2`. The footnote states that the PRU-baseline entry (35)
  and the Emax entry (2.2, logit scale) are standard deviations. The PD reading
  is supported by the concentration-response and steady-state quantiles above,
  which reproduce the published medians and IQRs to within a few percentage
  points. The PK etas cannot be checked as directly; the alternative reading
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)` would change only the spread, not the medians.
* **Molecular weight.** The paper does not print it. The ticagrelor value
  522.57 g/mol reproduces the printed `Css,av` of 576 and 864 nmol/L exactly.
* **Molar metabolite formation.** `Fm` is applied as a molar fraction, and the
  metabolite states hold ticagrelor-equivalent mass. The paper does not say
  whether the NONMEM dataset used molar doses; the molar reading gives the
  metabolite-to-parent exposure ratio of 0.36 ("approximately one third").
* **Erlang chain.** "Eight transit compartments", with the same KTR used from
  the dose compartment to the first transit compartment, between transits and
  from the last transit to central, is encoded as `depot -> transit1 ... transit8
  -> central`, with nine transfers at rate KTR.
* **Lag time.** Applied to the dose compartment for prior-MI (PEGASUS)
  patients only, as Table 2 reports it.
* **Study and population.** The PEGASUS-TIMI 54 substudy is the only source of
  prior-MI patients, so the study indicator `STUDY_PEGASUS` carries both the
  lag time and the lower PRU baseline.
* **Below-LOQ data.** The authors fitted below-LOQ PK samples with the M3
  method; that is an estimation feature and does not affect simulation.
* **Not modelled.** Clopidogrel PRU data (summarised descriptively by the
  authors) and the VerifyNow BASE channel (used only for graphical display).
* **Figure 4 boxes.** The boxes in the published Figure 4 look slightly wider
  than the IQRs quoted in the Results text; the simulation is compared with the
  text values.
